_doc: Pebblebol FINAL content set. Every constant the battle, progression, breeding, corruption and encounter code reads. 1:1 with plan 1.5.2.
_TYPE_CHART_doc: TYPE_CHART[attacker][defender]; SIGNAL>CORRUPT>SYSTEM>SIGNAL, +1/0/-1 (spec 12). A NEUTRAL attack never indexes this table: its modifier is 0 unconditionally, so there are still exactly three damage types and the chart stays 3x3.
_TYPE_MOD_MAX_HITS_doc: THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX, and the part no draft had. A per-hit damage edge COMPOUNDS: over the ~5 exchanges a fight lasts, even a modifier small enough to be invisible on a 5-point hit decides the duel. Measured: with the modifier uncapped, every visible multiplier lands the cross-type cells at 69-78% (and the plan's additive +-2 at 86-92%). So the modifier is capped: an attacking Pebble gets TYPE_MOD_MAX_HITS type-modified hits per battle, and after that its mod is forced to 0. One u8 counter per battle side, never persisted. It is also the right fiction for this game - you exploit the weakness once and then it is patched - so the battle log reads '!Exploit!' on the modified hit and nothing after. With the cap at 1 the six off-diagonal 1v1 cells land at 40-63% and the 3v3 lead advantage at 57-65%.
_TYPE_MOD_doc: THE FIX FOR THE ONE THING ALL THREE DRAFTS GOT WRONG. plan 1.5.2 writes damage = max(1, power*atk/(def*K)) + 2*type_mod + rng(0..2). Hits land for 4-8 points, so a flat +-2 is a 50-100% swing and the triangle decides the fight (measured off-diagonal win rates of 88-98% in all three drafts). Here the modifier is MULTIPLICATIVE and applied to the raw term before the rng: dmg = max(1, raw * TYPE_MUL_NUM[mod+1] / TYPE_MUL_DEN[mod+1]) + rng(0..2), indices 0/1/2 = mod -1/0/+1. Integer arithmetic, two 3-entry int8 tables, no FPU. TYPE_MOD_SCALE is kept as a real key (graft: draft_B-balance): set TYPE_MOD_MODE=ADDITIVE and TYPE_MOD_SCALE=2 to restore the plan's original formula for an A/B run in P9-C4.
_XP_TABLE_deleted_doc: THE PACK'S 31-ENTRY XP_TABLE (inc(L) = 25 + 12*(L-1) + 4*(L-1)^2, total 36,453) AND ITS XP_TOTAL_TO_MAX WERE DELETED HERE BY P9-C4, which is the chunk the plan sequenced the decision into after P4-C1, P4-C6 and P9-C3 each deferred it. The firmware compiles ONE curve, and it lives in Pebblebol/src/data/balance.h: 10 + L*L, total 8,845. Two curves in two files was the second source of truth this deletion ends, so DO NOT ADD ONE BACK - verify.py now reads the shipped curve out of balance.h and FAILS BY NAME if an XP_TABLE key reappears here. THE EVIDENCE, from tests/tools/sim_days.cpp over 30 simulated days of the real game/sim.cpp, game/xp.cpp and game/encounters.cpp: measured XP/day is 18.8 (light, 2 device-ON h), 109.4 (normal, 8 h and balance.h's own 3-4 touches), 352.8 (heavy, 14 h) and 1,031.9 at the physical ceiling. Against the plan's 3-4-week target the shipped curve reaches level 30 in 25 days of heavy play and 81 of normal; the pack's needs 103 days of heavy play and 333 of normal, and does not reach the band even at the unreachable ceiling (35 days). Note also that game/sim.cpp's v1 stage clock writes level 20 into PebbleInstance.level after 3.5 days on zero XP, so the first 2,660 points of the shipped curve (10,963 of the pack's) are free either way.

FORMULAS.damage: max(1, raw * TYPE_MUL_NUM[mod+1] / TYPE_MUL_DEN[mod+1]) + rng(0..2), where mod is forced to 0 once the attacker has already spent TYPE_MOD_MAX_HITS type-modified hits this battle
FORMULAS.accuracy_eff: max(ACCURACY_MIN, accuracy - EVASION_PER_SPD * min(EVASION_MAX_SPD_GAP, max(0, spd_def_eff - spd_atk_eff))); non-damaging moves are never dodged
FORMULAS.protect: incoming = max(1, incoming >> 1) while PROTECT_HALF is active
FORMULAS.buff: one stage = +/-1 on the raw stat for effect_duration rounds; stages clamp to [-2,+2]; stats floor at 1
FORMULAS.priority: higher priority acts first; ties by effective spd; spd ties by the shared battle Rng
FORMULAS.dot: effect_value damage at end of each round for effect_duration rounds; ignores DEF and PROTECT, and NEVER STACKS - re-applying refreshes the duration. Stacking DOT on a high-DEF Pebble is the one degenerate kit the matrix found (a stage-2 TANK went to 100%).
FORMULAS.corrupt_status: EFF_CORRUPT gives the TARGET the spec 55 modifier for effect_duration rounds: +1 ATK stage, -1 DEF stage. See CORRUPTION.
FORMULAS.switch: switching consumes the whole turn (spec 14) and resets the switched-in Pebble's stages to 0
FORMULAS.budget_cost: budget_cost = power*accuracy/100 + 12*max(0,priority if power>0 else 0) + effect_weight(effect,value,duration) - min(12, 4*cooldown) - 2*recoil/3, clamped to >= 1
FORMULAS.capture_permille: CAPTURE_BASE_PERMILLE[wild.rarity] - CAPTURE_LEVEL_GAP_PERMILLE*max(0, wild_level - active_level) + CAPTURE_VALUE_SCALE*item.value, clamped to [CAPTURE_MIN_PERMILLE, CAPTURE_MAX_PERMILLE]
FORMULAS.evo_cond_units: HAPPINESS_GE percent 0..100; ACTIVITY_GE hours of lifetime_active_s; BATTLES_WON_GE count (reserved, unused by the built-in roster); ITEM item id; CORRUPTED 0
FORMULAS.special_xp: SPECIAL_XP_SCALE * event.value, withheld while the clock is CAL_UNSET

_EFFECT_WEIGHTS_doc: budget_cost is COMPUTED from this table for every row in attacks.json and for every creator move, so the built-in roster and a custom Pebble are priced by one rule (spec 36). Never hand-typed. Priority is charged on offensive moves only - charging it on PROTECT prices defensive archetypes out of the game (finding grafted from draft_B-balance).
_ITEM_VALUE_doc: ItemDef.value is a uint8_t in the 8 B struct, so it carries a MAGNITUDE whose unit depends on klass: XP_CANDY value*XP_CANDY_SCALE = XP granted (5/24/100 -> 40/192/800); CAPTURE value = capture-chance bonus in PERCENT, scaled to permille by CAPTURE_VALUE_SCALE (15/45 -> +150/+450 permille, which is what the Spanish flavour line has always promised the player); CARE value = care points restored (0 = the item is a key, not a consumable effect); BATTLE_MOD value = stat stages granted at battle start. No shipped value exceeds 255, and verify.py asserts it - so the table generates without widening the struct. If a later item needs > 255 the schema fix is to spend one reserved byte on a u16 value; do NOT invent a second out-of-band scale constant.
_EVASION_doc: Under the plan 1.5.1 formulas SPD does nothing but break turn order, so a FAST or EVASIVE Pebble pays 6-7 of its 16/22/28 stat points for a tiebreak. Measured cost: the FAST archetype won 24% of stage-0 duels and EVASIVE 31% before this rule existed. Evasion gives SPD a second job: an attack's effective accuracy is max(ACCURACY_MIN, accuracy - EVASION_PER_SPD * min(EVASION_MAX_SPD_GAP, max(0, spd_def_eff - spd_atk_eff))), i.e. at most -30 points. Utility moves are never dodged. One integer line in the battle resolver, and it is what makes a four-stat system have four stats. P9-C4 RAISED EVASION_PER_SPD FROM 2 TO 3 (cap -20 -> -30) against the SHIPPED engine rather than this model. tests/tools/balance_matrix.cpp fought all 3,600 ordered pairs of the 60-species roster 1,000 times each at level 15 through game/battle.cpp and game/battle_ai.cpp and found the rule still undersized: SIGNAL carries 11 of the 12 SPD archetypes and CORRUPT 13 of the 13 ATK ones, so a rule that underpays SPD reads as a TYPE imbalance. Measured same-stage cross-type win rates at 2: SIGNAL 42.9 %, CORRUPT 56.8 %, SYSTEM 50.3 %, with 9 of 60 species outside 35-65 % against their own stage. At 3: 46.6 / 55.0 / 48.5 and 5 of 60. At 4 the correction overshoots - SYSTEM sags to 46.8 % and two SYSTEM FAST bodies cross 65 % - so 3 is the measured answer and not the largest available one.
_RARITY_doc: Rarity has to mean something in the matrix or a HIDDEN-only trophy loses to a backyard common (measured in all three drafts: draft A's three specials were its three WEAKEST finals). It must not mean stat points, or totals decide the matrix. So rarity buys ATTACK BUDGET: a rare gets +8 and a special +16 on top of ATTACK_BUDGET_BY_STAGE, and the learnset search targets RARITY_TARGET_WINRATE instead of a flat 50%. verify.py asserts mean win rate is monotonic in rarity within each stage.
_LEARNSET_RULES: every move is the species' own type or NEUTRAL
at least one TYPED damage move
at least one NEUTRAL damage move (Choque or Apuesta) - the release valve, so no Pebble is ever left with a kit in which every attack is at a type disadvantage
at least one move whose category is not DAMAGE or RISK
_creator_doc: A custom Pebble is capped at the stage-1 budget so it can never out-stat a final evolution (spec 68 r17). Appendix C's POWER bar uses FORMULAS.creator_power_pct.
_starter_doc: Paketo: SIGNAL, common, stage 0, BALANCED 4/4/4/4 - the most ordinary creature the roster allows.

_ANIM_doc: AttackDef.anim_id is an index into ANIM_FILMS, NOT a per-attack id. Fourteen films, many attacks per film - that is deliberate, so P10-C3 writes fourteen renderers and not thirty-four. The film list is owned by P10-C3 (battle hit/faint/protect on rd_flash/rd_shake/rd_dither_rect, evolution dissolve, capture and item films on the actfx pixel writer). Adding a film appends an id; existing ids never move, so attacks.json does not churn when the renderer grows.
_ITEM_DROPS_doc: EncounterRow has no item id field, so an ITEM outcome is resolved here: pick uniformly by weight among the entries for the network category, then reject any item whose rarity falls outside the ITEM row's [rarity_min, rarity_max]. gen_content.py emits it as ItemDropRow { u8 category, item_id, weight, reserved; } (4 B x 33 rows = 132 B) - the one struct plan 1.5.2 is missing.

sprite_glitch._doc: P9-C5: petfx XOR-noise rows, 1 frame in 8. Three 24 px rows are XORed with a per-hour noise word, so the glitch is stable within an hour and moves between hours. Never touches the stored sprite.

CORRUPTION._idle_doc: altered behaviour (spec 55): the idle film swaps to IDLE_CORRUPT - the blink is replaced by a 1-frame horizontal tear and the walk cycle drops every fourth step.
CORRUPTION._infect_doc: corruption exists in BOTH loops: the SPECIAL encounter sets it for 24 h out of battle, and attack 12 Infectar applies it inside a battle. When a battle ends with the loser still carrying the EFF_CORRUPT status there is a 12.0% chance it persists as the 24 h status - that is the only way a battle can hand you an evolution.
CORRUPTION._doc: spec 55: corruption never destroys a Pebble. It is a signature mechanic, not an annoyance: it is the ONLY route to two of the sixty species.

BREEDING.eligibility: both parents compat_group equal, both stage >= 1, both level >= 15, both generation < GENERATION_MAX, Box has a free slot
BREEDING.offspring_species: stage 0 of ONE parent's family, chosen by a fair coin from RNG_BREEDING. Cross-family pairing inside a group is therefore the only way to farm a family you do not own a stage 0 of - that is what makes the groups mean something.
BREEDING.move_inheritance: the offspring starts on its own species learnset, then move slot 4 is replaced by one move drawn from the OTHER parent's learnset, if and only if that move is legal for the offspring (own type or NEUTRAL), respects POWER_CAP_BY_STAGE[0] and keeps sum(budget_cost) <= ATTACK_BUDGET_BY_STAGE[0]. Otherwise slot 4 is unchanged. Exactly one slot, never two.
BREEDING.stat_inheritance: NONE. base stats come from SpeciesDef and are identical for every instance of a species. The only per-instance variation is Genome (0..2 per stat, plan 1.5.1) and it does NOT grow with generation.
BREEDING.trait_inheritance: 50/50 from either parent, or none if neither has one
BREEDING._ceiling_doc: spec 17's hard balance ceiling, stated as three numbers: base stats are never inherited (so no escalation is possible at all), genome variation is capped at GENOME_VAR_MAX and is generation-independent, and at most INHERITED_MOVE_SLOTS move crosses over. Generation is capped at GENERATION_MAX so the lineage_id chain in the 16 B Genome cannot be farmed indefinitely.
BREEDING._group_design: each group deliberately spans at least two of the three types, so a cross-family pairing inside a group can be same-type (the offspring may inherit a TYPED move) or cross-type (only a NEUTRAL move can cross). verify.py asserts the spread.

STRING_CONTRACT._doc: plan 1.5.2 types name_idx and flavor_idx as StrId indices, and strings_es.h states an ORDERING CONTRACT (grouped blocks index-parallel to the enums in nt_types.h). Section 53 forbids Spanish literals anywhere else. This is how the 60 names, 60 flavor lines, 34 attack names and 10 item names get interned - the single largest piece of unwritten work between these JSON files and a compiling species_table.h.
rules: the four blocks are APPENDED to strings_es.h in that order, after every existing StrId, so no existing index moves and the ordering contract holds
gen_content.py emits src/data/content_strings.h with the four BASE constants and static_assert(STR_ITEM_NAME_BASE + 10 == STR_COUNT)
name_idx and flavor_idx are NOT carried in the JSON because they are derivable from id; verify.py re-derives them and checks contiguity

encoding is Latin-1 (RD_FONT_BODY = u8g2_font_5x8_tf, 191 glyphs). Accents and n-tilde are REQUIRED, not optional: strings_es.h already ships 45 accented UI lines and the roster must not read worse than the menu around it

HANDOFF_INVARIANTS: species.id is contiguous 1..60 and equals index+1
sprite_id == id - 1, so SPRITE_SETS is a flat 60-entry array walked straight off species.json and tools/gen_sprites.py needs no lookup
evo_rule == (family-1)*2 + stage for stage 0 and 1, and 255 for stage 2
EvolutionRule[i].species is the species whose evo_rule is i
attack.id and item.id are contiguous from 1
anim_id is an ANIM_FILMS index, not an attack id (see _ANIM_doc)
_ITEM_TARGET_doc: ItemDef.target and ItemDef.param are the two columns P4-C1's completeness pass found MISSING (plan line 552): a CARE item did not say WHICH of the five care stats it restores and a BATTLE_MOD did not say which stat, for how long. target is klass-scoped - CARE reads it as CARE_TARGET_ENUM (ALL restores all five), BATTLE_MOD as BATTLE_STAT_ENUM (which is game/battle.h's BattleStat ordering, not a second one), and every other klass carries NONE == 0. param is one byte with one meaning per klass too: CARE puts the PEBBLE_STATUS_BITS mask it also clears there (items.json 'clears'), BATTLE_MOD puts the buff's length in ROUNDS there (items.json 'duration'), and no row may set both. A CARE item's value is PERCENT OF FULL: care[] is 0..PB_CARE_MILLI_MAX milli-points, so value 40 means +40 % of a full bar, which is the only reading a uint8_t can carry against a 100000-point scale.
_CAPTURE_doc: spec 23. base by the WILD species' rarity, minus CAPTURE_LEVEL_GAP_PERMILLE per level the wild creature is ABOVE the active one (never a bonus for being below - 'failure should not feel excessively punishing' is not the same as free), plus CAPTURE_VALUE_SCALE * the capture item's value, clamped to [CAPTURE_MIN_PERMILLE, CAPTURE_MAX_PERMILLE] so no catch is certain and none is impossible. CAPTURE_MAX_ATTEMPTS failures and the creature flees.
